system.name: DPA-Store
system.one_liner: a NIC-resident ordered key-value store that answers requests on-path using a learned index, running on a SmartNIC's DPA cores

components.name: Host DRAM
components.role: host memory accessible via DMA from the SmartNIC

components.name: eSwitch
components.role: embedded switch that steers packets within the BlueField-3

components.name: DPA
components.role: on-path Data Path Accelerator cluster (16 RISC-V cores) that processes packets and can DMA to host memory

components.name: DPA memory
components.role: memory local to the DPA cores

components.name: ARM
components.role: off-path ARM CPU that runs a dedicated OS for control-plane management and accelerator access

components.name: Network fabric (Ethernet, InfiniBand)
components.role: external network the SmartNIC's RX/TX ports connect to

flows.what: direct memory access (DMA) to host memory over PCIe
steers incoming RX packets to the DPA cores

content.key_idea: The BlueField-3 SmartNIC pairs an on-path DPA core cluster with an off-path ARM control CPU and its own DRAM, and in NIC mode the DPA can DMA results directly into host memory.
content.reading_order: Top-down: host CPU/DRAM, across the PCIe bus, into the BlueField-3 package (eSwitch, DPA, ARM, NIC DRAM), down to the network fabric.

evidence: it offers an off-path ARM CPU and an on-path DPA cluster
The DPA subsystem consists of 16 physical RISC-V cores, each running at 1.8 GHz
The ARM CPU allows the BlueField-3 to run a dedicated operating system

summary: This is a background figure explaining the NVIDIA BlueField-3 SmartNIC that DPA-Store, an ordered network-datapath key-value store, is built on. Drawn as a layered stack, a host CPU and Host DRAM sit above a PCIe bus, below which the BlueField-3 package contains an eSwitch, an on-path DPA cluster (16 RISC-V cores at 1.8GHz) with its own DPA memory, an off-path ARM CPU for control-plane management, and 16GB of NIC DRAM; RX/TX ports connect down to the Ethernet/InfiniBand network fabric. A DMA arrow crosses the PCIe boundary to Host DRAM, illustrating that in NIC mode the DPA can write results directly into host memory, a capability DPA-Store's host-side tree updates rely on.

notes: Background hardware figure (BlueField-3 platform); DPA-Store's own architecture is shown separately in Figure 3 of the same paper.
